a.summary: MAIN FIX NOT APPLIED TO NEW CODE. Same defect as the previous entry in the second, hand-inlined instruction walk: the program-id index is read with `decode(data, o)` + `getByteLen(data, o)` instead of a raw u8. Beyond corrupting the price/limit offsets, a mis-advanced cursor also miscounts `numNonComputeBudgetInstructions`, which feeds the default-compute-unit-limit estimate, so the derived priority fee can be wrong in both factors.

b.summary: MAIN FIX NOT APPLIED TO NEW CODE — same defect as the previous entry, in the second hand-inlined instruction walk, and likewise not covered by any existing test. The program-id index is read with `decode(data, o)` + `getByteLen(data, o)` instead of a raw u8. Beyond corrupting the price/limit offsets, a mis-advanced cursor also miscounts `numNonComputeBudgetInstructions`, which feeds the default-compute-unit-limit estimate, so the derived priority fee can be wrong in both factors.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
